scope: PR-cycle security verdict for release 0.5.0 (rc-1 = final rc). Re-key of the T-050-36 review (f3e13023, APPROVED-PENDING-REKEY, snapshot 343acc38) onto HEAD 14ec830c, plus a diff-based review of the delta 343acc38..14ec830c (13 commits, 44 files, +3324/-518). verdict_reason: No blocking security or privacy finding stands against the HEAD tree at 14ec830c. None of the mandatory REQUEST_CHANGES triggers fires: public-asset privacy clean (`dadaia public doctor` → [ok] public-privacy, [ok] entities-derivation, 0 drift/missing); zero secrets, emails, IPv4 literals, home-abs-paths or private-key blocks across the delta's 3324 added lines; zero foreign-repo-slug hits against the gate-equivalent 10-slug foreign set (the single raw hit was the workspace's OWN slug, which the gate correctly excludes); no dependency added (pyproject delta is the version line alone); no CI workflow YAML touched; no mode/exec-bit change; no generated-file or consumer-data leakage. The six security findings routed for fix (F-13, F-14, F-16, F-17, F-18, F-20) are verified landed at 7280856c, each carrying a regression seam, and the F-14 fallout (M-8) is closed at 0246bbae; 52 targeted tests pass. CONDITIONAL ON THE OPERATOR'S HISTORY REWRITE (see finding 2): the push gate still blocks on 11 historical objects, none of which is in the HEAD tree; after the rewrite every sha in the range changes and THIS VERDICT MUST BE RE-KEYED to the new HEAD.

findings.message: HEAD TREE IS CLEAN — all 11 push-gate offending objects are historical, and the delta introduced zero new ones.
findings.detail_md:
Re-ran the new-branch push-gate simulation exactly as the pre-push hook runs it:

```
printf 'refs/heads/feature/0.5.0 %s refs/heads/feature/0.5.0 0000000000000000000000000000000000000000\n' "$(git rev-parse HEAD)" | <ws>/.dadaia/.venv/bin/dadaia ci push-gate-check   # BLOCKED, 11 objects
```

Count unchanged from the f3e13023 review (11), and every object classified:

| Class | Count | Classification evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Superseded blob (not the HEAD blob for its path) | 8 | each flagged blob id compared against `git rev-parse HEAD:<path>` — all 8 differ; e.g. `specs/bugs/BUGS.jsonl` flagged blobs `1a53838dd027`/`067f11a3711f`/`3122160426f5` vs HEAD blob `fa02026bddaa` |
| Commit message | 3 | `a0caa28eb22b` (operator denylist), `ffe1b00982e8`, `e5fa1fbf2677` (baseline `email-address`) — all three verified `git merge-base --is-ancestor <c> 343acc38` → true, i.e. **at or before the prior review's snapshot**, so the delta added none |
| HEAD-tree blob | **0** | no flagged blob id equals a HEAD blob for the same path |

**Independent whole-tree cross-check** (audit-lane posture, out of diff scope, recorded for completeness): running the packaged scanner (`features/chokepoints/denylist_scan.scan_objects`, 18 operator terms + 8 baseline patterns) over all 1773 HEAD-tree blobs raw — i.e. ignoring the gate's range/newness semantics — surfaces 40 raw matches. **Zero** of them are in a file the delta changed, 37 are byte-identical to `origin/develop`, and the 3 in branch-modified files (`tests/integration/test_public_assets.py:193`, `tests/unit/test_public_assets.py:30`, `tests/unit/test_backlog_models.py:66`) carry line content that is present verbatim on `origin/develop` — pre-existing, already-published synthetic scanner fixtures. Raw values redacted throughout; terms appear only in the scanner's own masked `t…n` form.
findings.fix_recommendation: No action on the code. The 11 objects dissolve with the operator's planned history rewrite — see the next finding for its blocking condition.

findings.message: F-01 CARRIED FORWARD — the history rewrite is deferred to the operator, must reword three commit MESSAGES (not just blobs), and this verdict must be re-keyed afterwards.
findings.detail_md:
CWE-532 (Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File). **Blocking for the push, not for the code.** The agent cannot perform this rewrite; it is the operator's.

Three of the eleven offending objects are **commit messages**, which a rewrite that only rewrites trees/blobs leaves published:

- `a0caa28eb22b` — line 4, operator denylist term. This is the very commit that removed the real operator term from the test fixtures, and it **names that term in its own message**.
- `ffe1b00982e8` — line 5, baseline `email-address`.
- `e5fa1fbf2677` — line 3, baseline `email-address`.

**Re-key condition (mechanical).** A history rewrite changes every sha in the range, including `14ec830cf1b6ae76ed19d37aef342fde1d82ef3e`. `metrics.commit_sha` in this handoff would then name a commit that no longer exists on the branch, and `.github/scripts/pr-verdict-check.sh` fails closed on it (`git cat-file -e -- <sha>^{commit}` → SKIP, then `no APPROVED security-reviewer verdict covers PR head`). This verdict therefore does **not** survive the rewrite by design.
findings.fix_recommendation: Operator: (1) rewrite the range with `--reword` on all three commits above, not merely `--amend` of their trees; (2) re-run `dadaia ci push-gate-check` and require **exit 0** before the first push; (3) re-dispatch `security-reviewer` to emit a NEW APPROVED verdict handoff keyed to the post-rewrite HEAD, committed at `specs/releases/0.5.0/verdicts/<new-head-sha>.handoff.json`. Do not open either PR on a range whose gate still exits non-zero.

findings.message: F-13/F-14/F-16/F-17/F-18/F-20 verified fixed at 7280856c — every fix is a deletion or a routing through an existing primitive, and each carries a regression seam.
findings.detail_md:
Diff-reviewed each fix against the finding it closes:

| Finding | Fix | Shape | Regression seam |
|---|---|---|---|
| F-13 (CWE-1188) | `features/backlog/document.py:665` — `denylist_terms` is now a required keyword-only parameter; the `= ()` default is **deleted** | deletion | 4 test call sites updated to pass it explicitly; mypy --strict now enforces at every future call site |
| F-14 (CWE-367/CWE-662) | `backlog_new` (`:576-589`) and `remove_active_subsection` (`:650`) route through `core.atomic_write.atomic_write(..., expected_previous=...)`; two bespoke `read_text`→`write_text` pairs deleted | routing to an existing primitive | `ConcurrentModificationError` surfaced verbatim, never swallowed. Verified `atomic_write` treats a missing target as `""` (`core/atomic_write.py:105-110`), so the fresh-file path with `expected_previous=""` is correct, not a spurious refusal. `features → core` is a legal edge under ARCHITECTURE P-04 |
| F-16 (CWE-1220) | `pr-verdict-check.sh:213-252` — every glob hit's release-id **segment** is validated against `_RELEASE_ID_RE`; strip prefixes derived from the canon templates, never a second hardcoded literal | added validation, no new trust root | `test_arm3_ideas_direct_verdicts_dir_refused_fails_closed` — asserts `no candidate verdict files found` for a `verdicts/` dir placed directly under `_ideas/` |
| F-17 (CWE-183) | `_is_verdict_evidence_path()` (`:182-203`) replaces the `case` glob whose `*` crossed `/`; the dead pre-v6 `specs/_archive/releases/*/verdicts/*` arm **deleted** | deletion + anchoring | `test_arm6_verdicts_shaped_path_outside_the_id_position_still_disqualifies` — asserts `specs/releases/0.5.0/reviews/verdicts/evil.py` still disqualifies |
| F-18 (CWE-20) | `pr-verdict-check.sh:92-96` — `PR_HEAD_SHA` shape-checked as 40-hex before it reaches any git argv | 4-line symmetry with the existing `metrics.commit_sha` check | `test_arm8_symbolic_pr_head_sha_refused_before_any_git_argv` — asserts `PR_HEAD_SHA=HEAD` is refused **and** that `PASS` never appears |
| F-20 (CWE-538) | `.gitignore:136-196` — `local-notes.md`/`tmp/` scratch denies carried to `specs/audits/**`, `specs/ADRs/**`, `specs/bugs/_archive/**`, `specs/backlog/_archive/**`, `specs/_archive/**`; plus a **latent ordering defect** the fix uncovered: the `specs/releases/**` denies sat BEFORE `!/specs/releases/_archive/**`, so last-match-wins silently undid them for every archived release — moved after | one line per area + a reorder | `git check-ignore` assertions in `tests/contract/test_source_repo_hygiene.py` |

Verified ordering hazards in the fixed script: the `_archive` arm of `_is_verdict_evidence_path` is tested first and a 5-segment archive path can never fall through to the 4-segment live arm; `_RELEASE_ID_RE` is the canon-derived anchored ERE, so `_ideas`/`_archive`/traversal tokens can never match.

**Fallout closed.** F-14 introduced a new exception type into two writers; `0246bbae` (code-review M-8) adds the fourth `except ConcurrentModificationError` arm in `cli/commands/newartifacts.py:156`, shaped identically to its three siblings (`[error] {exc}` + exit 1) rather than an uncaught traceback. Checked the other new raiser: `remove_active_subsection`/`backlog_exit` have **zero production call sites** (`grep` over `dadaia_workspace/` returns only docstring cross-references in `container.py:292` and `features/backlog/doctor.py:350`), so no second uncaught path exists today.

`pytest -p no:cacheprovider` over the five security-relevant suites — `tests/contract/test_pr_verdict_check_gate.py`, `tests/contract/test_source_repo_hygiene.py`, `tests/unit/features/backlog/test_document.py`, `tests/integration/cli/test_cli_newartifacts.py`, `tests/unit/core/test_atomic_write_census.py` — **52 passed**.
findings.fix_recommendation: None — accepted as landed. When `backlog_exit`/`remove_active_subsection` gain their first production caller, that caller must handle `ConcurrentModificationError` the way `backlog_new_cmd` now does.

findings.message: Bug-surface axis (FR24 / dd-bug-registration §5): the delta REDUCES the bug surface of every feature it touches.
findings.detail_md:
Assessed against the standing order (permanent architecture review, oriented by bug history), not against “tests green”.

- **`features/backlog/document.py`** — F-13 deletes a default that silently reintroduced `backlog-histo-writer-skips-write-time-denylist-redaction`, a bug this same release fixed; F-14 deletes two bespoke `read_text`→`write_text` writers and routes them through the release's own `atomic_write` primitive, closing the lost-update class `bugs-record-store-append-clobbers-concurrent-update-batch` was raised for. Both are **net deletions of a code path**, not additions.
- **`.github/scripts/pr-verdict-check.sh`** — F-17 deletes a `case` glob and a dead pre-v6 legacy arm, replacing them with one anchored predicate; F-18 adds four lines that make an existing asymmetry symmetric. F-16 is the only net-additive change, and it removes a trust root rather than adding a branch to a feature.
- **`.gitignore`** — F-20 fixes a latent last-match-wins ordering defect that had silently un-ignored scratch paths for every archived release. Pure correction.
- **`cli/commands/newartifacts.py`** — M-8 adds a fourth `except` arm, shaped identically to its three siblings. This is the one addition in the delta; it is consistency completion for an exception type F-14 introduced, not a new semantic path, and it has no alternative (the only other raiser has zero production callers).

No puxadinho: no flag, no second code path, no cross-feature reach-in, no new shared mutable state. Ledger context: 515 records, 8 open, 489 resolved (`dadaia bugs stats`).

**Method and limitations.** Diff-based per `DADAIA.md` §7; whole-tree observations are labelled audit-lane and pre-existing where recorded. `gitleaks`/`trufflehog` are **not installed** on this host — the secret pass used the persona grep patterns plus the packaged `privacy_baseline.json` `secret-token` pattern; a `gitleaks` run before the first push would be a cheap additional layer. **No exploit code was run**; the gate's pathname-expansion behaviour was re-verified only through the committed contract fixtures, never against this repository. All raw values are redacted — denylist terms appear only in the scanner's own masked `t…n` form, and no matched secret, email, path or private name is reproduced anywhere in this handoff.
findings.fix_recommendation: None — recorded as the FR24 axis this verdict is required to state.
